statements.statement: Total revenues for FY27 stated at $51,331,000, largely property tax (71%).
State aid figure used for the FY27 revenue projection, carried at the FY26 actual/cherry sheet level pending the Governor's budget.
Proposition 2 1/2 automatic increase added to the FY26 levy limit to build the FY27 levy limit.
New growth for FY27 estimated at $400,000 by the assessors, added to the levy limit.
After subtracting FY26 appropriations from available FY27 revenue, the amount left for all new costs (town, school, every contract) as heard.
Under the traditional proportional apportionment of new revenue, the school would get $696,521 above FY25.
Under the traditional proportional apportionment of new revenue, the town would get about $573,000 above FY25.
Under the traditional proportional apportionment of new revenue, Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical (Monty Tech) would get $36,000.
School department's projected health insurance increase for FY27 stated at $740,000.
Town side's projected health insurance increase for FY27 stated at $480,000.

After subtracting the projected health insurance increases from all new FY27 revenue, only $86,000 remains for every employee, every vendor, every new item townwide and schoolwide, before Monty Tech's assessment is even known.
Lunenburg has been told to budget health insurance at a 20% increase for FY27.
An 'outside' (worst-case) override/gap figure of $1,464,000 given as one number in the school-side summary.
